lessonActivities.title: Prepositional Phrases with At and By – Your First Step! 🎯
lessonActivities.content:
Welcome to Prepositional Phrases! These are set expressions that add meaning to sentences. 📚

What are they? Fixed combinations of preposition + noun/gerund that have special meanings.

PrepositionCommon PhrasesMeaning
Atat an advantage, at a disadvantage, at any costhaving benefit/loss, no matter what
Atat a distance, at easefar away, comfortable
Byby accident, by all accounts, by all meansunintentionally, according to reports, certainly
Byby chance, by handaccidentally, manually

Try it: Sophie is at an advantage. I found my ring by accident.
examples: Sophie's computer skills puts her at an advantage.
Eva is at a disadvantage without computer skills.
We must avoid the spread of the virus at any cost.
The policeman followed the suspect at a distance.
I was immediately at ease with the group.
I found my ring by accident when tidying the wardrobe.
By all accounts this is the best hotel in the area.
You may have a copy by all means.
He met her by chance in a bookshop.
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Practice Tip: Learn phrases in context, not isolation.

lessonActivities.title: Phrases with In and On – Building Confidence 🚀
lessonActivities.content:
Great! Let's add more useful phrases to your toolkit. 📈

More phrases: These help express ideas like addition, timing, and reasons.

PrepositionCommon PhrasesMeaning
Inin action, in addition, in advancedoing something, also, before time
Inin agreement, in caseagreeing, if something happens
Onon account of, on average, on behalf ofbecause of, typically, for someone
Onon display, on edgebeing shown, nervous

Example: It's amazing to see the sculptor in action. The paintings are on display.
examples: It's amazing to see the sculptor in action.
We get a bonus at the end of the year, in addition to our salary.
Passengers should book well in advance.
We were in agreement with his analysis.
Take a sweater in case it gets cold.
He couldn't speak on account of a sore throat.
It takes 5 minutes, on average, to walk to the station.
I'm making this request on behalf of all the members.
His paintings are on display at the moment.
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Memory Aid: Group phrases by preposition to memorize.

lessonActivities.title: Phrases with Out, Under, Within/Without – Advanced Usage 🔍
lessonActivities.content:
You're doing awesome! Let's master the final phrases for complete fluency. 🎭

Advanced phrases: These add nuance to your English.

PrepositionCommon PhrasesMeaning
Outout of bounds, out of breath, out of controlbeyond limits, breathing hard, uncontrollable
Outout of dangersafe now
Underunder age, under consideration, under controltoo young, being thought about, managed
Underunder discussionbeing talked about
Within/Withoutwithin earshot, within reason, without doubtclose enough to hear, reasonably, certainly
Within/Withoutwithout delayimmediately

Example: The patient is out of danger now. The proposal is under consideration.
examples: Paul sent the ball out of bounds.
Julia ran all the way home and arrived out of breath.
The children were totally out of control.
The patient is out of danger now.
Children under 18 are under age.
The boss said that her proposal was under consideration.
There were some violent protests but the situation is now under control.
The work is under discussion.
He made sure the boss was not within earshot before speaking.
I agree with the proposal within limits.
The author is without doubt one of the greatest writers.
We must find a solution without delay.
lessonActivities.tips: 💡 Practice Tip: Create sentences using multiple phrases.

lessonActivities.title: Complete List of Prepositions – Mastery Level 🧠
lessonActivities.content:
Review the complete list of prepositions and their uses. 📘

Core Concept: Prepositions show relationships between words in sentences.

Categories: Position, Direction, Location, Time, etc.

Complete List: above, across, after, against, along, among, around, as, at, before, behind, below, beneath, beside, besides, between, beyond, but, by, concerning, considering, despite, down, during, except, for, from, in, inside, into, like, near, of, off, on, onto, out, outside, over, past, regarding, round, since, through, throughout, to, toward, towards, under, underneath, until, up, upon, with, within, without.

Examples: The coconut was high above our heads. We walked across the street.
examples: The coconut was high above our heads, so nobody could reach it.
The cat lay across my lap.
We walked across the street.
After dinner, we ate dessert.
The broom was leaning against the fence.
The path led along the river.
The deer hid among the trees.
There was a white fence around the house.
We don't have a coffee maker at work.
Before work, I go to the fitness center.

quizActivities.question: What does 'at a glance' mean?
quizActivities.hint: At a glance means seeing something immediately.
quizActivities.explanation: At a glance means to see or understand something quickly.

quizActivities.question: Choose the correct phrase: 'The proposal is ___ consideration.'
quizActivities.hint: Under consideration means being thought about.
quizActivities.explanation: Under consideration means currently being discussed or evaluated.

quizActivities.question: What does 'without doubt' mean?
quizActivities.explanation: Without doubt means there is no question about it.
